Then step (j)'s Core 11 reading turns PASS and CVG-021 is re-derived to CONFORMS.

Verify with: `uv run evaluations/turnkey/run.py --env local --steps j --workspace ~/dev/hw-converge --project converge`

title: The operation kit judges the lanes at work; the lanes that reported back are unjudged
description:
Filed while closing converge-q66 on 2026-09-04.

The operation payload now carries lanes in two lists: `lanes` (at work, read in the lane words Working / Quiet / Silent — may have died) and `reported` (already come back, read in the work words Done / Stuck). That split is what lets `experience-operation.v1` Core 8 be kept without stretching a three-word vocabulary over a state it has no word for.

`conformance/experience-operation/run.py` reads only `op["lanes"]`:

- rule 8 checks the state word and the evidence of the lanes at work, and never looks at `reported`. A reported lane could carry any word at all, or no evidence, and the kit would still report PASS.
- rule 9 (Watch session) counts `lanes` without a session; a reported lane whose session is still alive is offered a Watch control that no rule checks.

Owner: whoever owns `conformance/experience-operation/`.

Suggested fix: rule 8 also asserts that every entry in `reported` reads one of the work words `experience.v1` Core 6 fixes (Done · Stuck) and carries evidence; and that no lane id appears in both lists, so the split cannot be used to hide a lane from either check.
acceptance: GIVEN an operation payload whose `reported` list carries a lane with a word outside the work vocabulary, or no evidence, or an id that also appears in `lanes` WHEN the kit runs THEN it reports FAIL naming that lane.

title: test_console_live_rendered's "a line typed in the browser arrives" fails under machine load
description:
`app/tests/test_console_live_rendered.py::test_a_line_typed_in_the_browser_arrives_in_the_manager_session` failed once during converge-9mq and passed everywhere else, and the difference was how busy the machine was.

Measured 2026-09-04 on lane/w8-writes-named:

* Full suite WHILE three other browser jobs were running on the same host (this lane's own verification script, a falsification run, and a second pytest): **1 failed, 291 passed**, with

      assert page.evaluate("() => document.querySelector('#consoleForm input').value") == ""
      AssertionError: a delivered line clears the field; a kept line would mean it was not sent
      assert 'ZZTYPEDINBROWSERZZ' == ''

  Its own captured output shows the line DID arrive - `tmux -L cvlive capture-pane` printed `ZZTYPEDINBROWSERZZ` twice, and `console errors: none`. So the delivery worked and only the field-cleared assertion was early.

* The same test alone in this tree: **1 passed**. The same test alone at the merge base a06d970 in a scratch worktree: **1 passed**. The full suite again on a quiet machine, same commit: **292 passed**.

So the assertion reads the input's value at a moment that is not guaranteed - the field is cleared when the send resolves, and under load the read can beat it. Nothing in this lane's change touches the console (`console.html`, `render/console.js`, `tmux.js` are all untouched; the diff is the shell rail, two templates, one stylesheet and a new test file).

Ten lanes on one machine is the normal case here, so a test that only holds on a quiet host will keep costing someone a false red. The fix is to wait for the field to clear rather than read it once - e.g. `page.wait_for_function("() => document.querySelector('#consoleForm input').value === ''", timeout=...)` - which fails just as loudly when the line genuinely was not sent.</parameter>
<parameter name="acceptance">GIVEN the app test suite runs on a host that is busy with other browser work WHEN `test_a_line_typed_in_the_browser_arrives_in_the_manager_session` runs THEN it passes whenever the line does reach the tmux session, and still fails when it does not - the delivered-line assertion waits for the field to clear rather than sampling it once.

title: The constraint strip's fix has no test — nothing stops it being clipped again
description:
Contract: platform-web.v1 §14 — "it renders at 390 and 1280 pixels with nothing cut off and nothing overlapping" (ledger row CVG-213, which no scan can settle).

converge-6qk fixed the workspace header's constraint strip: its three chips (HARD LIMIT / STRATEGY / LANES) were being swallowed by `overflow:hidden` at every width. The fix is three CSS declarations in `app/static/css/shell.css`. Nothing in the repository would notice if a later change undid it — the whole defect lived for weeks precisely because no check looks at rendered geometry.

That lane owned only `app/static/css/shell.css`, so it could not add the test. The harness it used is complete and working, and was left uncommitted at `ai_working/w8-shell-css/measure_strip.py` in the lane worktree (lanes/w8-shell-css). It follows the shape of the existing `app/tests/test_console_overflow_rendered.py`: an in-process app server, a Playwright Chromium context per width, and a MANUAL_PROCEDURE that stands in when Playwright is unavailable.

What it measures, per width and per console state: each chip's box against the strip's padding box (that is where `overflow:hidden` clips), each chip's own text overflow, the strip against the viewport edge, whether the objective spills out of its own box, and whether the objective and the strip actually overlap on both axes. It carries a realistic long objective, because the defect only appears when the objective is long enough to win the flex fight.

Widths that matter: 390 and 768 (the strip is hidden below 980), then 1000, 1100, 1200, 1280, 1440, 1600, 1920. The 1000–1200 band is the one that catches the interesting failure — the naive one-declaration fix passes at 1280/1440/1920 and produces a 1127px-tall header at 1000 with the console open.</description>
<parameter name="acceptance">GIVEN the app test suite WHEN it is run with Playwright available THEN a rendered test asserts that all three constraint chips are fully inside the strip's clip box at 1000, 1280, 1440 and 1920 with the console both open and closed, AND it fails if the strip's `flex:0 0 auto` or the header's `flex-wrap:wrap` is removed, AND it skips with a printed reason plus a manual procedure when Playwright is unavailable.

Contract: platform-android.v1 §1-§9 - the whole contract, ratified DRAFT 2026-09-03.

the contract's nine clauses can be checked. The nine ledger rows (CVG-240 to CVG-248)

The clauses describe a bottom navigation bar, notification channels, the system back gesture, a share target, a widget or quick-settings tile - all of them shapes a real Android application
takes. None of that can be judged from a file scan, a route table, or the
companion web page; it needs the body itself.

Making these checkable therefore means building the body, and that is a
sub-project rather than a lane in this queue: its own repository, its own
steward, and its own Converge instance with its own ledger derived from this
same contract. Filed so the debt is visible in one place, and parked in the
same breath so nobody mistakes it for work that can start here.

Derived 2026-09-04 by the gap analysis in docs/workflow/GAP-ANALYSIS-2026-09-04.md.
acceptance: GIVEN a Android body built against experience.v1 and platform-android.v1 WHEN a conformance kit for that body runs against it THEN each of the nine clauses is either kept, with a rule that can tell a right body from a wrong one, or says in plain words what a machine cannot settle about it. Until such a body exists there is nothing here to start.

title: Steward decision + ready-to-file upstream issue: bkrabach/amplifier-bundle-converge@main ships a session-wide spawn: block
description:
RESIDUAL from converge-w3v. The cause is outside this repository, so this lane proved it and stopped. Two things are needed from the steward: a decision, and (if the decision is "fix the fork") the issue text below, which is written to be pasted as-is.

WHAT WAS MEASURED (2026-09-04, this host, control/treatment/attribution/removal-control; every row is the composed mount plan's `spawn` plus the tool modules a spawned helper inherits per the shipped apply_spawn_tool_policy):

  A control  -- unrelated `anchors` session, nothing composed:
      spawn: null   helper keeps: tool-bash, tool-delegate, tool-skills
  B treatment -- the same session as this host composes it (22 app bundles):
      spawn: {"exclude_tools": ["tool-delegate","tool-skills","tool-bash"]}
      helper LOSES all three
  C attribution -- each of the 22 app entries composed alone; exactly ONE carries a spawn policy:
      git+https://github.com/bkrabach/amplifier-bundle-converge@main#subdirectory=behaviors/converge.yaml
      (microsoft/amplifier-bundle-converge, installed on the same host, is clean: spawn null)
  D removal control -- the host app list MINUS that one entry:
      spawn: null   helper keeps all three, 22 tool modules

Reproduce: `uv run conformance/composition/run.py .` in this repo; rule 6c now reports it by name.

THE DECISION (converge-w3v names three options; recommendation last):
  1. The fork drops the `spawn:` block (bundle.md:54 and behaviors/converge.yaml) -- fixes it for everyone who installed the fork.
  2. The entry is removed from this host's app list: `amplifier bundle remove` / edit ~/.amplifier/settings.yaml:27 -- fixes this host only, leaves the published bundle harmful.
  3. The steward rules the two Converge bundles are the same product and one is stale -- then 1 and 2 both follow.
  RECOMMENDED: 2 first (it is one line and immediate -- every session on this machine currently spawns helpers with no bash, no delegate, no load_skill), then 1 so the harm does not travel to the next person who installs the fork.
  NOT DONE BY THIS LANE: settings.yaml is host-wide shared state with other lanes live on it, and it is outside this lane's file ownership.

-- UPSTREAM ISSUE TEXT (paste into bkrabach/amplifier-bundle-converge) --

Title: A session-wide `spawn.exclude_tools` strips bash, delegate and load_skill from every spawned helper in every session on the host

Installing this bundle with `--app` takes tools away from sessions that have nothing to do with Converge.

`bundle.md:54` (and the same block in `behaviors/converge.yaml`) declares:

    spawn:
      exclude_tools:
        - tool-delegate
        - tool-skills
        - tool-bash

An app bundle is composed onto EVERY session (amplifier_app_cli/runtime/config.py hands `get_settings().get_app_bundles()` to `load_and_prepare_bundle` as `compose_behaviors`), and `spawn` lands in the composed root mount plan. `apply_spawn_tool_policy` then filters those modules out of the parent tool list on every spawn -- for all agents, in all sessions, not just Converge's.

Measured on a host with this bundle app-installed (control, treatment, attribution, removal control -- full numbers above): an unrelated `anchors` session's spawned helper loses tool-bash, tool-delegate and tool-skills. Removing this one entry from the app list restores them; no other one of the 22 installed app bundles declares a spawn policy at all.

The block's comment calls it the "GUARANTEED path" for the agents' negative-capability contracts. It is -- it guarantees them for everybody's agents, in everybody's sessions.

Ask: drop the `spawn:` block from both files. Per-role spawn tool policy is the upstream feature request this needs (see microsoft/amplifier #388); until it lands, agent tool limits belong in the agents' own `tools:` blocks and body instructions.

For reference, microsoft/amplifier-bundle-converge removed exactly this block on 2026-09-02 after measuring the same harm, records the rule in PINS.md ("Never reintroduce a session-wide `spawn:` block"), states it as a contract clause (composition.v1 Core 6), and as of 2026-09-04 has a standing conformance rule (6c) that fails when an app-installed release of the product strips a neighbour's tools.
acceptance: GIVEN this host WHEN `uv run conformance/composition/run.py .` is run in amplifier-bundle-converge THEN rule 6c reports PASS -- the unrelated session's mount plan carries no session-wide spawn.exclude_tools and its spawned helper keeps tool-bash, tool-delegate and tool-skills -- which becomes true once either the fork drops the block or the entry leaves the host's app list. Falsified by 6c still reporting FAIL and naming an app-installed release of this product.

title: The Direction header shows the whole objective sentence, so it grows to a third of the screen
description:
Contract: platform-web.v1 §14 (nothing cut off, nothing overlapping) — this is not a breach of it, it is the cost of keeping it, and it is a design call someone should make deliberately.

`#objectiveText` in `app/templates/direction.html` is filled with the first sentence of the batch's Outcome section (`app/data.py`, `manager_card`). In the real batch that sentence is 270 characters. The header renders it in full at 16px with no clamp, so the header's height is a function of how much someone wrote.

Measured in Chromium against a realistic objective, before and after converge-6qk's strip fix (header height, console open):

  1000  233px -> 261px
  1100  186px -> 238px
  1200  163px -> 215px
  1280  140px -> 215px
  1440  140px -> 215px
  1600  117px -> 163px
  1920  117px -> 117px

The growth is real and was accepted knowingly: before the fix the header was shorter because two of the three constraint chips were not being drawn at all. But 261px of a 800px viewport is a third of the screen spent on a band that is meant to be a summary, and the document surface below is the actual work.

Options a steward or the owning lane might weigh: clamp the objective to two lines with the full text one gesture away; take a shorter objective from the batch; or accept the height as the honest price of showing all three constraints. This lane owned only `app/static/css/shell.css` and could not touch the template or the payload, so it recorded the number rather than choosing.</description>
<parameter name="acceptance">GIVEN the Direction view at 1280px with the console open and a 270-character objective WHEN the workspace header is rendered THEN the header occupies no more than a stated, deliberately chosen height, AND the full objective text is reachable without leaving the view, AND all three constraint chips remain fully readable.

title: Seven operation clauses have no runner — the turnkey's nine steps exercise none of them
description:
Contract: operation.v1 — Core 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 11, 13, and its own "Conformance kit asserts" list.

The turnkey harness (evaluations/turnkey/run.py) went green on 2026-09-04 and the steward ratified the sentence recording it into the contract. Its nine steps assert: a fresh environment, one install, the install check, a project started, work derived from a contract gap, two real lanes, integration, a re-check, and a return brief.

Seven Core clauses are exercised by none of those steps. Re-derived from a live observed run on 2026-09-04 (`uv run evaluations/turnkey/run.py --env local --workspace ~/dev/hw-converge --project converge --steps e,f,g,h,i`), each row's probe reads only whether modes/converge-manager.md still carries the clause's section — which is the mode encoding the rule, never the manager session following it:

    CVG-012  Core 2   the plan is visible — order, dependencies, collisions, opportunistic picks, with reasons
    CVG-013  Core 3   never the bottleneck — work that proceeds without the steward is maximised
    CVG-014  Core 4   feedback is signal — evidence quoted, reports merged and split before filing
    CVG-016  Core 6   width is a collision decision — lanes fill only with items that provably touch different files
    CVG-019  Core 9   stalls are decisions — no progress across iterations becomes stuck with cause
    CVG-021  Core 11  four calls reach the steward — anything else is a defect to file
    CVG-023  Core 13  hand off when done — a manager session that has lost its footing writes a hand-off and stops

Each is a promise about what a manager session DOES across a wave, and each needs an observation nothing currently takes. Some are cheap (clause 6: compare the files two concurrent lanes own against the launcher's manifest; clause 13: count hand-offs against manager sessions that ended by choice). Some need counting events across a whole wave (clause 3, clause 11 — evaluations/ratchet already counts owner-facing prompt events, but for the reconciler, not for a manager session). Clause 4 needs a raw report and its filed item side by side.

Discovered while re-deriving fifteen ledger rows for converge-0gb. These seven were red pending the turnkey; the turnkey is green and does not touch them, so the reason they are not yet kept has changed and is now written down.

Whoever takes this should not assume one lane closes all seven. Pick the ones an observation can reach, and say plainly which are left.

title: Direction: restore can only reach the steward's read point, not an arbitrary history snapshot
description:
Contract: experience-direction.v1 section 6.

Section 6 asks that restoring from history be a real action at four scopes. converge-wrx made it one: the History view now offers Restore at wording, paragraph, section and whole-document scope, and each is the app's own changes/{change_id}/restore write, one sentence at a time — committing on a draft, writing a proposal beside a locked document.

What it cannot reach is any snapshot other than the steward's own read point. The only sentences app/changes.py can still find are the ones in the current reading (the diff between the read point and HEAD), so a History row older than that read point has no restorable wording behind it. The panel says this plainly on the screen rather than implying time travel it does not have.

Closing this needs server files no Direction lane has owned so far — app/serve.py and app/writes.py. The design field carries the smallest shape that works; it is two optional parameters, not a new subsystem.

Found while working converge-wrx; filed rather than made, because the routes are another lane's files. Confirmed still true and still out of reach by lane w8-direction-polish on 2026-09-04, which owns only the browser half (app/static/js/**, app/templates/direction.html, app/static/css/direction.css) and deliberately did NOT ship a control with no route behind it. The acceptance was lost into this description when the item was first filed; it is in its own field now, unchanged in wording.
acceptance: GIVEN a document with several commits in its History WHEN the steward picks a snapshot older than their read point and restores at any of the four scopes THEN the document (or, if locked, a proposal beside it) carries the wording as of that snapshot, and the History panel no longer says arbitrary snapshots are out of reach.
design:
Measured while working w8-direction-polish, 2026-09-04. The restore machinery ALREADY works for an arbitrary snapshot: app/changes.py's changes_for(repo, path, since=<sha>) and find_change(..., since=<sha>) take any commit, and a card's `before` is exactly the wording as it stood at `since`. What is missing is only a way for the browser to name one — app/serve.py hard-codes `since` to the steward's stored read point in both document() and _reword().

So the smallest honest shape is two optional parameters, and app/writes.py need not change at all (apply_change already takes the resolved card, and already makes the lock check that decides commit-vs-proposal):

1. GET /api/managers/{mid}/docs/{repo}/{doc} accepts an optional ?since=<sha>, used INSTEAD of the stored read point for that one response. It must not move the read point: the read point belongs to the steward, and reading history is not reading.
2. POST .../changes/{change_id}/restore (and /edit, for the same reason) accept an optional `since` in the body, passed straight to changes.find_change.

Bound both: `since` must be one of the shas data.history_for(repo, path) returns for THIS document, else refuse in plain words — "that is not a commit in this document's history". A route that reads any revision the caller names is a different, larger promise than section 6 makes.

Browser half, once the route exists (all inside the Direction lane's own files — app/static/js/render/direction.js, actions.js, api.js): the History row already selected in state.historyId carries its sha; restorePanel reads the document at that sha to list the four scopes against it, each restore write carries the sha, and the Details paragraph naming this item is deleted. app/tests/test_direction_polish.py::test_the_history_panel_still_says_what_a_restore_cannot_reach pins the honest sentence today, and is the test to delete in the same commit that makes that sentence false.

Also worth knowing: app/README.md ("History: restoring, at four scopes") names converge-4pq as the open gap, so this item's id is load-bearing in shipped documentation and in the screen's own words. Whoever closes this updates both.

title: CVG-020: repoint the probe at the returns-vs-briefs count the mode now produces
description:
Contract: operation.v1 Core 10 — "A brief on every return."

converge-823 built the missing half: `modes/converge-manager.md` clause 10 now makes the manager session stamp the return in the log's entry heading the moment the steward's message arrives (`## <date> <HH:MM> — <headline>`), and write the five parts under it as labelled sentences at the end of the turn. Written at two different moments, returns and briefs are now countable against each other. That lane owns the mode and the log only, so the ledger row was left untouched — this is the hand-off.

CVG-020's probe today asserts `MODE-ENCODES-CLAUSE-10-LOG-EXISTS-BRIEFS=9` — briefs with no denominator. The replacement counts both sides. Run verbatim by `bash -c` from the repo root, as ledger/checks/verify.py runs refs:

```
if grep -q "^## Clause 10 - " modes/converge-manager.md && grep -q "Stamp the return before you answer it" modes/converge-manager.md && [ -f docs/workflow/OWNER-RETURN-LOG.md ]; then awk 'function f(){if(e_){r++;if(a&&b&&c&&d&&x)br++}a=b=c=d=x=0} /^## [0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9] [0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]/{f();e_=1;next} /^## /{f();e_=0;next} e_&&/\*\*Time away\.\*\*/{a=1} e_&&/\*\*Finished\.\*\*/{b=1} e_&&/\*\*Stuck\.\*\*/{c=1} e_&&/\*\*Needs you\.\*\*/{d=1} e_&&/\*\*Anything quietly broken\.\*\*/{x=1} END{f();print "MODE-STAMPS-RETURNS RETURNS=" r+0 " BRIEFS=" br+0}' docs/workflow/OWNER-RETURN-LOG.md; else echo STATE-CHANGED-REREAD-THIS-ROW; fi
```

Measured 2026-09-04 against the merged mode, the verbatim ref in a temp tree:

| log under test | output |
|---|---|
| the real log today | `RETURNS=0 BRIEFS=0` |
| one stamped return, five parts | `RETURNS=1 BRIEFS=1` |
| one stamped return, *time away* folded into *finished* (the defect a real manager session committed) | `RETURNS=1 BRIEFS=0` |
| two stamped returns, one never briefed | `RETURNS=2 BRIEFS=1` |
| an unprompted brief (date-only heading) | `RETURNS=0 BRIEFS=0` — not counted as a return |
| mode reverted, log perfect | `STATE-CHANGED-REREAD-THIS-ROW` |

The reading to record with it: the row turns green when RETURNS equals BRIEFS **and** RETURNS is above zero. Today it is 0/0 — the mechanism is encoded and the comparison is computable, but it has no denominator until a real manager session stamps its first return, so the row stays red on the same reason it has always been red, with the reason now one step shorter. It goes red the moment a stamped return goes unbriefed.

What the probe cannot prove, and the row should say so: a return the manager session never recorded at all leaves no trace either way. That is the honest limit of a record the returning session keeps itself. Closing it further would need a record of returns kept by something other than the session that returns.
acceptance: GIVEN ledger/rows.yaml WHEN CVG-020 is re-derived THEN its probe compares stamped returns against completed briefs (the ref above, or one that counts the same two numbers), its `expect` pins the count measured on the merged result, its `proves` says what the count cannot say, and `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` reports that ref meeting its expect. Falsified if the row still pins a brief count with no denominator, or if the new ref is pinned without being run.

title: A lane's plain state word reaches the screen in the machine's screaming form
description:
Found on 2026-09-04 while closing converge-d83 (the same defect, one element over).

`app/data.py` serves each lane a plain word — `statusLabel` is `Working` / `Quiet` / `Silent — may have died` for a lane at work, and `outcomeLabel` is `Done` / `Stuck` for one that has reported back. The payload is correct and `conformance/experience/run.py` rule 6a PASSes on it.

The screen is not. `app/static/css/operation.css:60` styles the pill that carries it:

    .lane-status { font-size:9px; text-transform:uppercase; ... }

so a steward reads `WORKING`, `QUIET`, `SILENT — MAY HAVE DIED`, `DONE`, `STUCK`. `DONE` is not `Done`: `experience.v1` Core 6 fixes the title-case word and the SCREAMING token is the machine's, which is the whole of the clause.

No rule catches it, and that is worth recording:

- rule 6a reads the payload, which is already plain;
- rule 6b scans served markup for the machine's tokens but skips `.css` routes (`conformance/experience/run.py`, `check_machine_vocabulary_is_folded`), and the token is never written down in the markup — the browser makes it at render time;
- `experience-operation` rule 8 reads the payload field too.

Same shape as converge-d83's second half: the wave phase was repaired in the payload AND had to opt out of `.wave-kicker`'s `text-transform:uppercase` before the plain word actually reached a person. The repair there is an inline `style="text-transform:none"` on the phase span in `render/operation.js`, because this lane does not own `operation.css`.

Two things to decide, not one:
1. the lane pill should stop upper-casing its word (the rule belongs in `operation.css`);
2. a rendered check should exist that would have caught it — `innerText` (text as RENDERED, transform applied), never `textContent` (text as written), which is how it survived a green suite. `app/tests/test_operation_plain.py` has the pattern.

Owner: whoever owns `app/static/css/operation.css` and the lane-card renderer.
acceptance: GIVEN the Operation page is open in a browser at 1280 and at 390 WHEN each lane card's state pill is read with `innerText` THEN every value is one of `Working` · `Quiet` · `Silent — may have died` · `Done` · `Stuck` exactly as written, and none is upper-cased.

title: Workspace header's constraint strip is cut off at every width — two of three chips never render
description:
Contract: platform-web.v1 §14 — "it renders at 390 and 1280 pixels with nothing cut off and nothing overlapping". Ledger row CVG-213 records that clause as one no scan can settle; this is a failure of it measured by hand.

Found while doing the rendered check for converge-c4s (console overflow) on 2026-09-03, in Chromium against the real app.

  1280 console open   -> 92px   all three chips clipped
  1280 console closed -> 138px  HARD LIMIT ok, STRATEGY + LANES clipped
  1440 console open   -> 102px  all three clipped
  1920 console closed -> 219px  HARD LIMIT ok, STRATEGY + LANES clipped

Not caused by the console lane: the strip clips identically with the console open and closed, and `app/static/css/shell.css`'s workspace-header rules are untouched on branch lane/app-overflow. Reported rather than fixed because this lane's brief scopes out any other visual change.

title: platform-web: offline the app shows nothing and says nothing
description:
Contract: platform-web.v1 §10, §11 ("Offline it reads what it last synced, and says when that was") and Core 11 ("Offline it refuses the five writes in a plain sentence").

Read from `app/static/sw.js` as committed:

    //   2. /api is network-first and is never written to the cache at all, so a stale
    //      decision or lane state can never be shown as if it were live.

That rule is a good one and it is the reason both clauses are unmet. Static assets are precached, so offline the shell loads — but every payload behind it comes from `/api`, which is never cached, so the shell renders empty. There is nothing that "was last synced" to read, nothing that says when, and no plain sentence refusing a write: `api.js` turns a failed fetch into a toast reading `Could not refresh: <message>`.

The two clauses and the service worker's rule are not actually in conflict — the clause asks for *what was last synced, labelled with when*, which is a different thing from a stale value shown as if it were live. Closing this is a design call about which payloads may be cached with a visible timestamp, not a one-line change.

Owner: whoever owns `app/`. This lane owns `ledger/` and `conformance/` only. No kit rule covers either clause today — no experience kit takes the network away — so the ledger rows are GAP citing this item rather than a rule id.

Ledger rows this closes: CVG-209, CVG-210. Grouped by cause and component on 2026-09-04 by docs/workflow/GAP-ANALYSIS-2026-09-04.md, which is where the whole mapping of rows to items is printed. The rows already named this item as their fix; what was missing was the list, written down here.
acceptance: GIVEN the installed app with the network off WHEN it is opened THEN it shows what it last synced with a visible "as of <time>", and any of the five writes attempted is refused in one plain sentence rather than a failed-request message.

title: Pinned open: the app now keeps a per-steward reading store, and experience.v1 clause 7 says it holds no data of its own (CVG-106)
description:
Contract: experience.v1 Core 7 — "**The app holds no data of its own.** It shows the project's documents, code record, work queue, lanes, return log, and pending decisions. A second copy of the truth is a defect, not a cache."

Measured 2026-09-04 (converge-dgc, the reconcile after wave 8). Since converge-f5f the app keeps `~/.amplifier/converge-app.state.json` (`app/state_store.py`, `--state` overrides the path). Read live on this machine: one steward, `stewards.bkrabach.read["amplifier-bundle-converge/vision"] = {"sha": "afd83c8b…", "at": "2026-09-03T23:25:47-07:00"}`, kept marks empty. Exactly two things per steward and nothing else — the read point (a commit sha the steward has read a document up to) and the kept marks (which changes that steward has said they are keeping). `app/README.md:38` already publishes it in the source-by-source table.

THE TENSION IS REAL AND THE CONTRACT ALREADY KNOWS IT. experience.v1's own Reserved / open questions section asks: "Where the reading cursor behind 'what changed since you last read' is kept, given the app holds no data of its own." That is this question, written by the contract's own author, unanswered.

Two facts pull opposite ways:
- The clause's teeth are kept. "A second copy of the truth is a defect, not a cache" — the store holds no document text, no work item, no lane state, no return log. A sha is a pointer into the truth, not a copy of it.
- The clause's letter is contradicted. The app does now hold a file of its own, per steward, outside the repository.

THE READING PROPOSED, for the steward to accept or reject: per-steward reading state is the STEWARD's, not the project's. Where you have read to is not a fact about the project — two stewards reading the same repository have different, equally correct answers, and neither belongs in the repository's history. Keeping it in the browser was considered and rejected in `app/state_store.py`'s own docstring, because the same person reads on a laptop and again on a phone and must see the same reading.

A CANDIDATE IS ALREADY WRITTEN: `contracts/experience.v1-candidate.md` now carries a second proposed change (clause 7) that distinguishes the project's truth — never copied — from the steward's own reading, kept per person outside the repository, and answers the Reserved question by name. It needs the steward's one word: *ratified · ratified with edits · declined · later*. Until then experience.v1 stands as the law and CVG-106 is OPEN-PINNED, asserting the current behaviour without forging the decision (PROTOCOL §3.3).

CVG-106's old probe passed on a stale proxy and would never have caught this: it grepped `app/*.py` for `sqlite3|shelve|pickle.dump`, and a plain JSON file is none of those. The rebuilt probe pins what the store actually holds — the path, the two-key vocabulary, and that no third module writes files — each break observed firing on a scratch copy 2026-09-04.
acceptance: GIVEN the steward has answered contracts/experience.v1-candidate.md's clause-7 change WHEN CVG-106 is re-derived THEN it carries CONFORMS against the ratified wording, or the reading store is gone and it carries CONFORMS against the current wording — not OPEN-PINNED either way. Falsified if the clause is left as it stands and CVG-106 is quietly returned to CONFORMS while ~/.amplifier/converge-app.state.json is still written.

title: CVG-186 goes red on main: the app's Ask write starts a second process, and it is not git
description:
Contract: experience-collaboration.v1 Core 7 — "**The manager session is not in the hot path.** A write made in the app goes through the ordinary repository and proposal mechanism directly; the manager session learns of it as an event and folds it into its next turn."

Measured 2026-09-04 on main tip 48cdc90 ("merge lane/w8-ask-route"), with no lane branch merged into it:

```
$ bash -c '<CVG-186's ref, verbatim>'
WRITES-START-A-PROCESS-THAT-IS-NOT-GIT
$ grep -cE "subprocess\.run\(" app/writes.py
2
257:        done = subprocess.run(
450:        done = subprocess.run(
```

At a1b7f82 (origin/main, the previous integration point) the same ref printed `WRITES-GO-STRAIGHT-TO-THE-REPOSITORY-GIT-ONLY` and `subprocess.run(` appeared once. The three commits that changed `app/writes.py` in between are afb1273, 672b6fc and 52452e1 — the Ask route. Two defensible readings — (a) the clause is kept, the probe is too narrow, and it should distinguish "a manager session" from "any subprocess"; (b) the clause is broken, because a write in the app now blocks on a session finishing. Whoever settles it owns both the row's re-derivation and, if (b), the app change.

Discovered by lane w8-ledger-followups while proving its own two rows against a scratch merge of main. That lane's brief is CVG-020 and CVG-114; re-deriving a third row it was not briefed for, on a reading it does not own, is the blind bump `ledger/rows.yaml` forbids — so it is filed. `app/writes.py` is also outside its file ownership.</description>

title: The app tests use one machine-wide tmux socket, so two suites at once break each other
description:
Found while running the app suite for converge-q66 on 2026-09-04.

`app/tests/test_tmux_view.py` opens its sessions on a fixed socket named `cvtest`, with fixed session names (`colors`, `tui`, `altscr`, `empty`, `marker`, `victim`), and its module fixture ends with `tmux -L cvtest kill-server`. Both names are machine-wide, so any two runs of the suite that overlap — ten lanes on one machine is the normal case here — collide:

    subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command '['tmux', '-L', 'cvtest', 'new', '-d', '-s', 'colors', ...]' returned non-zero exit status 1

Measured over five consecutive runs of `uv run --extra app --with pytest --with httpx pytest -q app/tests/test_tmux_view.py` while another suite was running: 15 errors / 3 failed / 8 failed / 15 passed / 15 errors. `tmux -L cvtest ls` showed the other run's sessions still alive at the moment of failure, and the second run's `kill-server` then takes the first run's sessions out from under it, which is where the varying middle numbers come from.

Nothing here is wrong with the code under test — `app/tmux_view.py` is not implicated, and the same file passes alone on a quiet machine. It is the fixture's naming. The consequence is that every lane's `pytest -q app/tests` verdict is unreliable while another lane is testing, which is exactly when a lane is deciding whether it is done.

Not fixed in this lane: it is not derived from converge-q66's gap, and the tmux view area belongs to converge-tfu.

Suggested fix: give the socket and the session names a per-run suffix (pid, or a uuid4 hex) so two runs cannot see each other, and scope the kill-server to that socket.
acceptance: GIVEN two runs of `pytest -q app/tests/test_tmux_view.py` started at the same time on one machine WHEN both complete THEN both report all tests passed, and neither leaves a session behind on another run's socket.

title: The host cannot reach its own webhook: /api/collab/webhooks/host is behind the sign-in gate, so polling is what actually keeps the surface fresh
description:
`experience-collaboration.v1` Core 6 asks for webhooks where the host offers them and polling as the honest fallback. Lane w8-collab-bridge built both: `POST /api/collab/webhooks/host` records an arrival and flips the surface's freshness sentence from "Polling - checked every 60 seconds..." to "Webhook - the host called this app at <stamp>...". It checks a shared secret read from `~/.amplifier/converge-app.webhook-secret` (`CONVERGE_COLLAB_SECRET_FILE` overrides), refuses 403 without it, and refuses 503 when no secret file exists rather than trusting the caller.

What it cannot do is be called by a real host. `app/serve.py`'s gate is a middleware over everything except `PUBLIC_PREFIXES` (`/login`, `/static/`, `/branding/`, `/favicon`, `/manifest.webmanifest`, `/sw.js`, `/healthz`), with no loopback exemption by design. A GitHub webhook carries no `cv_session` cookie, so it answers 401 and never reaches the route. Measured on 127.0.0.1:8846, 2026-09-04: with a cookie the route works end to end and freshness flips; without one the gate answers first.

So today the freshness that actually runs is polling, every 60 seconds, from `app/static/js/render/collab.js`. That is a kept clause rather than a broken one — Core 6 names polling as the honest fallback and the surface says which mechanism is carrying it — but the preferred half is unreachable, and this is where the remaining work is.

The change (`app/serve.py`, outside lane w8-collab-bridge's ownership): add `collab.WEBHOOK_PATH` to the public paths, and nothing else. The route's own shared-secret check is what stands in for the cookie — it must not be relaxed at the same time, or the app would gain an unauthenticated write.

Two things worth deciding at the same time, and both are steward-shaped rather than obvious:
- whether the secret should be an HMAC over the body (what GitHub actually sends, as `X-Hub-Signature-256`) rather than the plain shared header this ships with;
- whether the app is reachable from the host at all, which is a deployment question this repository has not answered anywhere.
acceptance: GIVEN the app is running and the webhook path is public WHEN a request carrying the shared secret but no session cookie POSTs to `/api/collab/webhooks/host` THEN it is accepted and the freshness sentence names the webhook; AND WHEN the same request carries a wrong secret or none THEN it is refused, and no other route has become reachable without a cookie.

title: The composition kit's two live rules still decline — nothing asserts helper reachability or the neighbour promise
description:
Contract: composition.v1 — Core 3 ("Its own helpers carry a small local rulebook … and borrow nothing else", judged live) and Core 6 ("Nothing touches the tools of other work in your session", judged live), and the contract's own "Conformance kit asserts" bullets 2 and 3.

Ran 2026-09-04, both rules, live:

    uv run conformance/composition/run.py . --json-only
      session_reaches_helpers        SKIP  "needs a live Amplifier session; this kit reads files only"
      unrelated_session_keeps_tools  SKIP  "needs two live Amplifier sessions (Converge plus unrelated work) side by side"

But a pinned decline is still an unasserted promise, and both of these promises are the ones that matter most: the second is the measurement that produced the PINS.md rule "Never reintroduce a session-wide spawn: block", taken once by hand on 2026-09-02 and re-taken by nothing since.

These two rows (CVG-008, CVG-009) named converge-qtp — the turnkey harness — as their fix, on the composition kit README's own reasoning that closing them "needs the live harness, not a cleverer file scan". converge-qtp is finished and its harness is green, and it does neither: its nine steps stand up an environment, install once, run the install check, start a project, derive work, run two lanes, integrate, re-check and brief. None of them asks whether a Converge session reaches a helper, and none stands a second unrelated session beside it.

So the fix these rows wait on is not the turnkey. It is either an extension of the turnkey (it already stands up a fresh container and installs into it — reaching a helper from inside is a small addition; a second session beside it is a larger one), or a separate two-session evaluation.

Discovered while re-deriving fifteen ledger rows for converge-0gb.

title: Nothing records a return, so operation.v1 Core 10's "a brief on every return" cannot be asserted
description:
Contract: operation.v1 §10 — "**A brief on every return.** Time away · finished · stuck · needs you · anything quietly broken — in sentences, appended to a log the steward can read."

Half of this clause is now kept and measurable: `docs/workflow/OWNER-RETURN-LOG.md` exists and carries nine dated briefs (measured 2026-09-04 by ledger row CVG-020's probe, `MODE-ENCODES-CLAUSE-10-LOG-EXISTS-BRIEFS=9`), and `modes/converge-manager.md` encodes the clause.

The other half is unassertable, and not for want of a probe. Nothing anywhere records that a RETURN happened — so no check can compare briefs to returns, and a count of briefs can never say whether one exists per return. Nine briefs against an unknown number of returns is a number without a denominator.

Two honest ways to close it, for whoever takes it:

1. Record the returns. If a return leaves a trace the steward's tooling can count (a line in the highway log, a session marker, a timestamped entry the manager session appends on wake), then the ratio becomes checkable and CVG-020 gets a probe that asserts the clause instead of half of it.
2. Decide the clause means the log, not the ratio. If "a brief on every return" is satisfied by the manager session's standing instruction rather than by a countable pairing, that is a reading the steward can ratify — and CVG-020 then re-derives to CONFORMS against the mode file plus the log, with the ratio recorded as out of scope.

Filed because CVG-020's `work` ref pointed at converge-qtp, which is RESOLVED — the turnkey harness landed. This ledger's own rule is that a closed item may not stay cited as the thing that will fix a red row, and the row needed a live item to cite. Discovered while reconciling after wave 7 (converge-nf4).

Not fixed here: that lane owns `ledger/**` only. The subjects are the mode file, the return log, and whatever would record a return.</description>
<parameter name="acceptance">GIVEN the repository WHEN operation.v1 Core 10 is checked THEN either a probe compares briefs in docs/workflow/OWNER-RETURN-LOG.md against a countable record of returns and finds one brief per return — or the steward has ratified, in writing, that the clause is kept by the mode's standing instruction plus the log, and ledger row CVG-020 carries that reading with a probe that asserts it.

Ledger rows this closes: CVG-020. Grouped by cause and component on 2026-09-04 by docs/workflow/GAP-ANALYSIS-2026-09-04.md, which is where the whole mapping of rows to items is printed. The rows already named this item as their fix; what was missing was the list, written down here.

title: CVG-020 is 0 of 0: nothing has stamped a return yet, so "a brief on every return" has no denominator
description:
Contract: operation.v1 Core 10 — "**A brief on every return.** Time away · finished · stuck · needs you · anything quietly broken — in sentences, appended to a log the steward can read."

converge-823 built the recording half: `modes/converge-manager.md` clause 10 now makes the manager session stamp the return in the entry heading the moment the steward's message arrives, and write the five parts under it at the end of the turn. converge-4xg (this lane) built the counting half: ledger row CVG-020's probe is now `ledger/checks/return_log_ratio.py`, which imports the turnkey harness's own `parse_return_log` and reports stamped returns against briefed returns.

2. The steward ratifies, in writing, that the clause is kept by the mode's standing instruction plus the log rather than by a countable pairing. CVG-020 then re-derives to CONFORMS against the mode file and the log, with the ratio recorded as out of scope.

The honest limit, recorded so nobody re-discovers it: a return the manager session never recorded at all leaves no trace on either side of the ratio. Closing that would need a record of returns kept by something other than the session that returns.

Filed because CVG-020's `work` ref pointed at converge-823, which is now RESOLVED, and this ledger's own rule (enforced by `ledger/checks/verify.py`) is that a red row may not cite a closed item as the thing that will fix it.</description>

title: CVG-046 goes red on main: the two new experience kits make it 7 of 7 aligned, and the row pins 5
description:
Contract: documents.v1 Core 5 ("The kit's rule table is numbered to these Core clause numbers, so a failing rule names the clause it breaks"). Ledger row CVG-046.

Measured in a scratch merge rather than guessed. lane/w8-step-regex merged into main at 1841b1b in a throwaway worktree, then the gate run there:

    uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py
      - CVG-046 expect NOT met (exit=0, stdout='KITS-ALL-NUMBERED-TO-CORE-CLAUSES=7')

The row expects `KITS-ALL-NUMBERED-TO-CORE-CLAUSES=5`. converge-f1l landed kits for experience.v1 and experience-collaboration.v1 (commits a693bcf, 5ae3d4e, 338b2e7), so there are seven kits now and all seven are aligned — the probe prints a count only when every kit is aligned, so 7 is the good answer, not the bad one.

This is drift TOWARD spec, and the row anticipated it in its own notes: "it goes red if any kit drifts, and it goes red if a sixth kit lands unaligned, which is the case that matters now that the experience family has three kits of its own."

Why it was filed rather than fixed by the lane that found it: ledger/ was lane w8-step-regex's file ownership, but that lane's tree has five kits, not seven. A row re-derived to pin 7 there would be red in that tree and green only after the merge — the same reasoning LEDGER-FORMAT and this ledger's own header apply to a SYNC pin: a lane whose tree holds the old bytes cannot honestly pin the new ones. It needs a tree that already has both kits.

Two things to check while re-deriving, not just the number: that all seven really are `aligned: True` (read documents kit rule 5b's own `observed` list, do not take the count on trust), and that the row's notes name which seven, as they name the five today.
acceptance: GIVEN main with seven conformance kits and CVG-046 pinning five WHEN the row is re-derived in a tree that actually has all seven THEN documents kit rule 5b's observed list is read and every kit in it is aligned, quoted in the row's notes by name; AND CVG-046's expect names the count that reading produced, with a RAN 2026-09-04 line saying what was run; AND `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` no longer reports CVG-046 in FAILURES.

title: The lock control's failure toast still says the app answers no lock route
description:
Contract: experience-direction.v1 §11 (the lock control) — and AGENTS.md §5, "never claim a result you did not observe", which cuts both ways: a screen may not claim a cause it did not observe either.

`app/static/js/actions.js`'s `sendLock()` catch reads:

    toast(`Nothing was locked — this app answers no lock route yet (${err.message}). Filed as converge-eci.`)

That was true while converge-eci was open. It is not true now: `POST /api/managers/{mid}/docs/{repo}/{doc}/lock` is answered by `app/serve.py` and written by `writes.lock_document()`, and the route refuses in plain words for real reasons — the document already carries a locking word, fewer than four conditions arrived, the document has uncommitted changes, it has no H1. Every one of those now reaches the steward under the wrong cause: they are told the app answers no lock route, when in fact it answered and refused, and it told them exactly why in `err.message`.

`app/static/js/actions.js` was outside this lane's ownership (writes.py, serve.py, api.js, render/direction.js, tests), which is why this is filed rather than fixed.

The fix is the catch body only — the success path is already correct and was measured working end to end. Something like: `toast(\`Nothing was locked — ${err.message}\`)`, so the server's own sentence is what the steward reads.</description>
<parameter name="acceptance">GIVEN a document that already carries a locking word WHEN the steward forces the lock control THEN the toast carries the server's own refusal naming that word, AND it does not say the app answers no lock route; AND a successful lock still reports the document locked.

title: app/tests/test_tmux_send_keys.py stomps a parallel lane: fixed tmux socket 'cvsend' plus kill-server
description:
Contract: operation.v1 (a check that cannot run says so, rather than reporting a failure someone else caused).

This is the twin of converge-bdc / converge-791, in a file lane w8-tests-isolation did not own and so did not touch. Those two items fixed `app/tests/test_tmux_view.py` and `app/tests/test_tmux_rendered.py`, which now take a per-run socket (`cvtest-<pid>-<random>`, `cvrender-<pid>-<random>`). `app/tests/test_tmux_send_keys.py` still opens its server on the fixed, machine-wide socket `cvsend` (line 44) with fixed session names (typist, closer, shortest, bulk, router) and a module fixture that begins and ends with `tmux -L cvsend kill-server` (lines 71, 81).

Measured 2026-09-04, after the other two files were fixed. Two `uv run --extra app --with pytest --with httpx pytest -q app/tests` runs started 0.5s apart on one machine:

  run A: 6 failed, 144 passed, 88 skipped  — all 6 in test_tmux_send_keys.py
  run B: 12 errors, 138 passed, 88 skipped — all 12 in test_tmux_send_keys.py
  failures in test_tmux_view.py or test_tmux_rendered.py, either run: 0

So the whole-suite verdict is still unreliable while another lane is testing, and it still points the losing lane at a file it never touched — just now at one file instead of three.

Fix, matching what the two sibling files already do:
1. `SOCKET = f"cvsend-{os.getpid()}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"` at module import (needs `import os`, `import uuid`). The convention and the measurement behind it are written down in `app/tests/conftest.py`, whose session-scoped reaper already kills and unlinks any socket carrying this run's pid — so nothing further is needed for cleanup.
2. Replace the `kill-server` at fixture setup with a refusal: if `tmux -L <socket> ls` succeeds, `pytest.fail` naming the sessions found, rather than killing a server this run did not start.
3. Wrap the session creation and the `yield` in `try/finally` so a `check=True` failure cannot skip the teardown.
4. Update the module docstring (lines 9-10), which currently states the socket is `cvsend`.</description>
<parameter name="acceptance">GIVEN two `pytest -q app/tests` runs started at the same time on one machine WHEN both complete THEN neither reports any failure or error in app/tests/test_tmux_send_keys.py, and neither kills the other's tmux sessions.

title: docs/work-items.json is stale, so the ledger's closed-cite tripwire is blind to converge-f1l
description:
Contract: documents.v1 (the kit's rule 9a reads the work queue through this export).

`ledger/checks/verify.py` carries a tripwire added by converge-0gb: no GAP/VIOLATION row may cite a work item that is already resolved, because "a reader who follows a closed cite lands on finished work and learns nothing about what would close the row". It reads `docs/work-items.json`, and an id absent from that export is reported as INFO rather than failed, on the stated ground that the export is a snapshot and a row may legitimately cite an item filed after it was taken.

That reasoning is sound and the export has now drifted far enough to defeat the tripwire in the other direction. Measured 2026-09-04 in this worktree:

  $ git log -1 --format=%ci -- docs/work-items.json
  2026-09-03 23:51:43 -0700
  $ python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('docs/work-items.json')); print(len(d))"
  76
  converge-f1l -> "open" in the export; RESOLVED in the live queue since
                  2026-09-04T10:56:59Z

So for a whole day the five rows citing converge-f1l (CVG-104, 107, 108, 112, 113) named a resolved item as their fix, and the tripwire built to catch exactly that reported OK — because the export still said the item was open. It answered from a stale snapshot with full confidence. That is the same failure shape converge-0gb was filed for, one layer down.

converge-5yu has now moved all five rows off converge-f1l, so the immediate lie is gone. The blind spot is not: nothing refreshes the export, and nothing says how old it is.

Also measured, and the smaller half of this: the export predates every item filed on 2026-09-04, so 15 red rows now cite ids absent from it (was 7 before this pass — converge-9mq, converge-er6 and converge-scb are all newer than the snapshot). Those are correctly reported as INFO. They are noise rather than error, but they are 15 rows the tripwire is not actually checking.

Two things would fix it, and they are separable:

1. Refresh the export — `uv run scripts/export-work-items.py --project converge --out docs/work-items.json`. A one-command fix that lasts until the next item is filed.
2. Make the staleness visible rather than silent — have verify.py print the export's own age beside the closed-cite verdict, so "no red row cites a resolved work item" is never read as stronger than the snapshot it was computed from. A check that quietly covers less than it says is worse than one that is absent; that sentence is already in verify.py's own comments, about a different tripwire.

Filed rather than made: `docs/` and `ledger/checks/verify.py`'s behaviour beyond the rows were outside this lane's file ownership (converge-5yu owns `ledger/**` only, and this is a `docs/` refresh plus a checker change).
acceptance: GIVEN docs/work-items.json is the snapshot ledger/checks/verify.py reads WHEN `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` runs THEN the export reflects the live queue's statuses (converge-f1l reads resolved, and every item filed to date is present) AND the closed-cite verdict is printed together with the export's own age, so a reader can see how far the check can actually see.

title: Offline: the service worker precache list does not carry app/static/js/presence.js
description:
`app/static/sw.js` is another lane's file, so this lane could not change it.

converge-wmh added `app/static/js/presence.js`, imported by `app/static/js/render/direction.js`. `PRECACHE` in `app/static/sw.js` lists every other client module by hand (`main.js`, `state.js`, `api.js`, `refresh.js`, `actions.js`, `offline.js`, and the four `render/*.js`) and does not list this one.

In practice the app is fine: `/static/*` is cache-first with runtime caching, so presence.js lands in the STATIC cache the first time it is fetched online, and `app/tests/test_offline.py` passes unchanged (verified 2026-09-04, 226 passed). The gap is the cold case the precache list exists for: a browser that installs the worker and goes offline before ever fetching presence.js would fail to import it, and direction.js would fail with it — taking the whole Direction surface down offline, not just presence.

Fix: add `'/static/js/presence.js'` to `PRECACHE` in `app/static/sw.js` (and consider whether the list should be derived rather than hand-kept, since this is the second module to be added since it was written).

Also noticed, same lane, same reason (not this lane's file): `app/tests/test_direction_writes_rendered.py`'s module docstring still says "Presence is this browser's own (converge-wmh). There is no channel that carries a second steward, so nothing here claims one." The first sentence is now false — the channel exists and `app/tests/test_presence.py` drives it across two browser contexts. The test body is unaffected and still passes.</description>
<parameter name="acceptance">GIVEN a browser that has installed the service worker and never fetched /static/js/presence.js WHEN it goes offline and opens the app THEN the Direction surface renders, because presence.js was precached alongside every other client module.

title: The app names no manager-session operation for any write, and states no limit for the two things it cannot do
description:
Two umbrella clauses about what the app *says*, both measured 2026-09-04 against the app at 127.0.0.1:8823 by `conformance/experience/run.py`. Both are the app's own surface to fix, and neither is this lane's file to touch.

**Core 8 — "Whatever you can do here, the manager session can do too."** Every write is meant to name the manager-session operation that does the same thing, so nothing the project needs is reachable only by a person at a screen. Rule 8 FAILs: this body offers four of the five writes (answer with a word · drop feedback · steer · ask for a proposal) and publishes no operation for any of them — no `data-manager-operation` attribute, no operations table in the client, no sentence naming one anywhere it serves. A reader cannot check the claim at all. (CVG-107 recorded the same gap from a hand-written probe; the superseded surface kit found the old app published this behind a Details fold, and the app that shipped does not.)

**Core 14 — "Where a body genuinely cannot do a thing, it says so in the app."** Rule 14 FAILs on two absences: there is no route for *raise or lower a priority*, and feedback is offered as text and as a screenshot but not as voice. The app says nothing anywhere about either — not what the limit is, not what to do instead. Silence is the only wrong answer the clause names.

The app already does this well elsewhere, which is why the rule can tell the difference: `render/direction.js` carries Details folds saying presence is this browser only and that restoring past the read point is not offered, each naming the item that would change it. The two absences above have no such sentence.

The priority write itself is a separate gap (Core 4, CVG-103, converge-6cc); this item is about the app being silent on it, not about building it.
acceptance: GIVEN the app is running WHEN `uv run conformance/experience/run.py <app>` is run THEN rule 8 PASSes — every write the body offers names the manager-session operation that does the same thing — AND rule 14 PASSes: for each thing the body cannot do, the app states the limit and what to do instead.

title: Rule 8a: no manager session names a steward — one field on the registration, in config.py and data.py
description:
`experience-collaboration.v1` Core 8 says whose word counts is settled when the manager session is registered, not inferred from whoever is signed in. `conformance/experience-collaboration/run.py` rule 8a reads `/api/boot` and looks for a key matching /steward/i on each manager. Measured live on 2026-09-04 against the app on 127.0.0.1:8846 with the collab router mounted: 8a is the only FAIL left in the kit (pass=11 fail=1 skip=2), reading "no manager session names a steward, so whose word counts is inferred from whoever is looking (this target answers as 'bkrabach')".

Lane w8-collab-bridge could not make this change: `app/config.py` and `app/data.py` are outside its file ownership. What it did instead is make the field the whole of the remaining work — `app/collab.py`'s `steward_of(mc)` already reads `getattr(mc, "steward", "")` and never falls back to the reader, and `app/tests/test_collab.py::test_one_steward_per_session_needs_one_field_on_the_registration` runs the contract's own kit over a boot payload carrying `steward` and shows 8a PASSing.

The change, in three places:

1. `app/config.py`, `ManagerConfig`: add `steward: str = ""`.
2. `app/config.py`, `_manager_from_table`: add `steward=str(table.get("steward") or "").strip(),`.
3. `app/data.py`, `manager_payload`: add `"steward": mc.steward,` to the returned dict.

Then one `steward = "<name>"` line per `[[managers]]` block in `~/.amplifier/converge-app.toml`, and a sentence in `app/README.md`'s "What it watches" paragraph naming the new key.

A manager block with no `steward` should keep answering with an empty string rather than guessing — an unregistered steward is a registration that has not been finished, and Core 8 is precisely about not inferring it.

title: The first check-record entry and the first stamped call on this host — clauses 7, 8 and 11 go from unread to a verdict
description:
Contract: operation.v1 — Core 3, 7, 8, 11. Ledger rows CVG-017, CVG-018, CVG-021.

Step (k) then reads the commit that introduced that entry and answers who verified. Continued: <what kept moving>.` in the plan record, at the moment of the call. Two of the four calls currently in HIGHWAY.md name which kind they are; the other two name none, which is why Core 11 is SKIP rather than a verdict.

Neither is new work in substance — clause 8 already says the verification is the manager session's own, and clause 11 already says exactly four calls reach the steward. What was missing was any trace afterwards, for somebody who was not in the session.

Verify with: `uv run evaluations/turnkey/run.py --env local --steps j,k --workspace ~/dev/hw-converge --repo <the integration checkout> --project converge`

title: Offline, a document's sync moment is in the banner and not on the document
description:
platform-web.v1 §10 says the helper "serves the documents already fetched, each marked with the moment it came from."

converge-719 delivers the moment for every stored payload, but shows it in one place: the offline banner, as a row of chips reading "vision as of 03:09 AM", "direction as of 03:09 AM", and so on. title: app/tests/test_tmux_view.py stomps a parallel lane: fixed tmux socket plus kill-server
description:
Contract: operation.v1 (a check that cannot run says so, rather than reporting a failure someone else caused).

Measured 2026-09-04 in lane w8-ask-route. Two runs of `uv run --extra app --with pytest --with httpx pytest -q app/tests` in this worktree reported failures inside `app/tests/test_tmux_view.py` — first 15 setup errors, then 2 assertion failures — while nothing in the run touched tmux code. Four later runs of the same command, and two runs of that file alone, all passed (15 passed, twice). The suite is green here.

The cause is shared state, not flakiness in the app: the module's autouse fixture runs `tmux -L cvtest kill-server` and then creates sessions named `colors`, `long`, `alt` on that same fixed socket. Every lane worktree runs the same command against the same socket, so two lanes testing at once kill each other's sessions mid-run. Ten lanes make this likely rather than rare.

The failure is worse than noise: it points a lane at a file it did not touch, and the honest reading ("someone else's run") is only available to someone who already knows the fixture uses a fixed socket.

Two ways out, both in the fixture: name the socket per-run (e.g. `cvtest-<pid>`), or refuse to run when a `cvtest` server is already up rather than killing it. The first keeps parallel runs independent; the second reports a collision instead of causing one.</description>
<parameter name="acceptance">GIVEN two `pytest -q app/tests` runs in different worktrees at the same time WHEN both reach test_tmux_view.py THEN neither kills the other's tmux sessions and both report their own result — and no run reports a failure caused by another run.

title: Guard: an H1 status of "(RATIFIED <date>)" is not recognised as locked, while "**Status:** RATIFIED" is
description:
Contract: composition.v1 clause 7 (structural enforcement of the proposal route) and documents.v1 clause 6 (status lives in the H1 and nowhere else).

Measured on the committed tree with the SHIPPED behaviors/converge.yaml config, calling the module's own functions:

  frozen_marker_regex : (?im)^\*\*Status:\*\*\s*(?:RATIFIED|FROZEN)|^status:\s*FROZEN|^#.*\(FROZEN\b

The three branches disagree about RATIFIED. The body branch accepts "**Status:** RATIFIED"; the H1 branch accepts only "(FROZEN". So a document that moves its status into the H1 - exactly what documents.v1 clause 6 mandates - and whose word is RATIFIED rather than FROZEN, reads as UNLOCKED where the same word in the body read as LOCKED.

docs/PROTOCOL.md is the live instance. Before this lane it carried "**Status:** RATIFIED - 2026-08-29" (regex matched). After the ratified v3 pass its H1 reads "# ... - Protocol v3 (RATIFIED 2026-09-03)" and no body status line remains, so the regex no longer matches at all:

  docs/PROTOCOL.md  matches guarded_globs: False  frozen_marker_regex: True -> '**Status:** RATIFIED'   [before]
  docs/PROTOCOL.md  matches guarded_globs: False  frozen_marker_regex: False                            [after]

Nothing changed in practice, because docs/PROTOCOL.md is not in guarded_globs (contracts/*.md, contracts/**/*.md, docs/VISION.md, VISION.md) and so was never guarded either way. The exposure is latent: the day a RATIFIED-in-H1 document is added to guarded_globs, the guard silently declines to guard it - the same under-match failure mode that produced converge-diw / -9vw / -ksg, and the reason the module README gives for making the H1 branch deliberately loose ("over-matching only ever guards more, whereas a guard that under-matches fails silently").

Decide one of: (a) teach the H1 branch RATIFIED as well as FROZEN, in the module default and behaviors/converge.yaml together (the test asserting they cannot diverge already exists); or (b) rule that RATIFIED is not a lock word, and record that where readers meet it.

Note: this item was filed with malformed markup that leaked stray tags into its own text and lost its acceptance field. This edit restores both.
acceptance: GIVEN a guarded file whose H1 carries "(RATIFIED <date>)" and which carries no "**Status:**" line WHEN a write to it is evaluated by hooks-candidate-guard THEN the outcome is the decided one - denied as locked, or documented as deliberately not a lock word - and the module default and behaviors/converge.yaml agree, proven by the existing divergence test.

title: No section contract tags a behavior with one of the four words, and none places one against the three surface classes

Many of the Before/Now are currently off by one, where one of the Now items was new and so then the next Now was lined up w/ the previous Before and so on. title: main.js still toasts "The console is read-only in this version" — unreachable today, false whenever it surfaces
description:
Contract: experience-console.v1 Core 3 and Core 9.

Discovered while closing converge-55b, which named this exact line as work outside its own file ownership. Lane w8-hygiene owns `app/templates/console.html`, `app/static/js/render/console.js` (note + disabled attribute), and `app/tests/test_console_input.py` only — `app/static/js/main.js` is another owner's file, so this is filed rather than fixed.

WHAT IS THERE, `app/static/js/main.js:149`:

    $('consoleForm').addEventListener('submit', (e) => { e.preventDefault(); toast('The console is read-only in this version.'); });

WHY IT IS NOT URGENT. It is unreachable. `app/static/js/render/console.js`'s `wireFurniture()` binds a `keydown` handler on the field (Enter, no Shift) and a `click` handler on the submit button, and both call `preventDefault()` before calling the console's own `sendLine()`. Neither path reaches a form submit, and those two handlers are wired unconditionally, not only when typing is live. Verified in a real browser at 1280 and 390 on 2026-09-04 against the app on 127.0.0.1:8873: typing is live, the send button is live, and the footer reads "not a chat — this pane is the manager session itself" at both widths.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS. The sentence is now false. The app has taken keystrokes since converge-tfu — `POST /api/tmux/{socket}/{session}/keys` answers, and `conformance/experience-console/run.py` rule 3 passes on it. Any future change that removes one of console.js's two `preventDefault()` calls, or that lands a submit path console.js does not own, surfaces a toast telling a steward the console is read-only while it is typing into their manager session. It is a false statement kept alive only by an accident of event ordering.

THE FIX, one line, either way:
- delete the handler outright (the two live handlers already cover Enter and the button), or
- make it call the console's own send instead of toasting.

Prefer deleting it: a second, differently-behaved submit path is the thing that would make this misfire in the first place.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS ITEM: grep for "read-only in this version" in `app/static/js/main.js` returning nothing.
acceptance: GIVEN app/static/js/main.js WHEN the console form's submit handler is read THEN it does not toast that the console is read-only — either the handler is gone, or it calls the console's own send; AND `uv run --extra app --with pytest --with httpx pytest -q app/tests` stays green; AND `uv run conformance/experience-console/run.py <running app>` still reports rule 3 and rule 9 PASS.

title: Experience kit rule 14: a body that merely says "voice is not offered" reads as offering voice
description:
Contract: experience.v1 Core 14 ("Where a body genuinely cannot do a thing, it says so in the app") and experience-operation.v1 clause 10 (feedback as text, a screenshot, or voice).

Rule 14 is coarse in BOTH directions, and each half was measured on this tree on 2026-09-04 while closing converge-9mq.

**1. A sentence saying voice is NOT taken reads as an offer.** The kit decides which feedback forms a body offers with FEEDBACK_FORMS — `("voice", re.compile(r"\bvoice\b|audio/\*|MediaRecorder"))` — matched against `served_text(snapshot)`, the shell plus every client asset. It cannot tell an OFFER from a STATEMENT OF ITS ABSENCE. Before converge-9mq, rule 14 reported `cannot_do: ['raise or lower a priority (priority)', 'feedback as voice']`; after adding the Core 14 sentence "a voice note is not recorded here", the word `voice` appears in what the app serves, so the form stops being counted absent at all and rule 14 reports `cannot_do: ['raise or lower a priority (priority)']`. The kit now has no rule that would notice voice going missing, and a body could satisfy the detector by writing the word `voice` in a comment. `<textarea` and `accept="image` are offer-shaped markers; a bare `\bvoice\b` is not.

**2. Any negation near the word counts as saying the limit.** `says_so()` passes if `\bnot\b|\bno\b|cannot|can't|does not|isn't|unavailable|not offered|not yet` appears within 220 chars of the thing's last word. Measured: with the whole limit sentence deleted from `app/templates/shell.html` — "This app has no control that raises or lowers a priority, and answers no route that would write one." — rule 14 still PASSed, satisfied by the surviving heading "Raise or lower a priority - not here". The clause asks for two things ("what the limit is, and what to do instead") and the rule reads only the first, loosely. `app/tests/test_writes_named.py` fences both halves for this body and does fail on that deletion; the kit should too, or the app half is the only thing holding it.

Not this lane's file (`conformance/` is owned elsewhere), so both are filed rather than fixed. A fix probably reads offer-shaped markers only for the forms (`audio/*`, `MediaRecorder`, a file input accepting audio), and asks `says_so` for a statement about the thing plus a second sentence naming what to do instead. The app's real voice gap is converge-rj1 and its real priority gap is converge-a5g; both should stay visible to some rule after this change.

title: lane-brief genre: an evidence-printing criterion must state the falsity condition, not only the presence condition
description:
Serves documents.v1. Ruled a brief defect (not a lane defect) by converge:protocol-authority, 2026-09-03, on review of lane w4-doc-kit-2's close.

WHAT THE BRIEF SAID

Lane w4-doc-kit-2's acceptance criterion 4 read, verbatim:

  "4. Both items resolved; each stored reason printed via work_list read-back."

WHAT HAPPENED

Both items were resolved and both reasons were printed — so the criterion was met exactly as written. But one of the two stored reasons contained a false paragraph, and the tracker will not let a resolution be corrected once an item closes (filed as work_tracker item work_item_pipeline-03c). The lane superseded the record and disclosed the defect, and the criterion still read PASS.

That produced a genuine, repeated disagreement about whether the lane had met its goal: the criterion's literal text was satisfied while its evident purpose — trustworthy evidence — was not. Under PROTOCOL.md section 7 the literal reading governs, because re-reading a briefed criterion at grading time to mean something stricter is a self-ratified amendment of the brief, which is forbidden to lanes and to the orchestrator alike. So the lane closed as SUCCESS-with-residual, correctly, and the ambiguity survived.

THE DEFECT

PROTOCOL.md section 4 requires a lane brief to carry an honesty gate: name what "not proven" looks like before work starts. Criterion 4 named what ABSENT evidence looks like — a reason not printed — and never named what FALSE evidence looks like. That omission is why the two readings could diverge at all.

THE CHANGE

The lane-brief genre should require that any criterion whose evidence is an artifact the lane itself authors states both conditions:

  - the presence condition: the artifact exists and is shown
  - the falsity condition: what makes the shown artifact unsound, and what the lane must do if it discovers its own artifact is wrong after it is written

Criterion 4 would then have read something closer to: "Both items resolved; each stored reason printed via work_list read-back; if a printed reason is found to be false, the correction must be reachable from the reason itself, not only from a linked item."

Applies to future briefs. It does not regrade w4-doc-kit-2, which finished against the version it was briefed on (PROTOCOL.md section 5).

The skill to change is skills/lane-brief.
acceptance: GIVEN the lane-brief skill WHEN an author writes a criterion whose evidence is an artifact the lane itself produces THEN the skill requires them to state what makes that artifact unsound, alongside what makes it present; AND it says what a lane must do when it finds its own evidence wrong after writing it; AND a worked example shows a criterion written both ways, so an author can see which one survives a lane that made a mistake and caught it.

title: infra_ledger.sh has no way to mark a registered server stopped, so every finished lane leaves an "open" row
description:
Found while finishing lane w8-tag-candidates (work item converge-er6).

The ten-lane-highway skill's `infra_ledger.sh` accepts `add|list|sweep` and nothing else. A lane is told to register its server on start and stop it before DONE, but there is no verb that records "stopped". Measured 2026-09-04:

    $ infra_ledger.sh <batch> done server w8-tag-candidates-app-8811
    ERROR: unknown command 'done' (want: add|list|sweep)

So `list` shows seven rows all marked `open`, six of them from lanes that have already finished and whose processes are gone. My own row reads `kill 2821616` and 2821616 no longer exists:

    2026-09-04T11:55:58Z  server  w8-tag-candidates-app-8811        open  kill 2821616

acceptance: GIVEN a lane has registered a server with `infra_ledger.sh add server <id> "kill <pid>"` WHEN the lane stops that server and records it THEN `infra_ledger.sh list` shows the row as no longer open, AND the ten-lane-highway lane instructions name the exact command that does it.

Deciding this is a documents.v1 amendment (a clarifying sentence in clause 4), not a code change. If reading (a) wins, rule 1b tightens to fail an extra section and operation.v1 needs an edit; if (b) wins, clause 4 should say so explicitly so the next reader does not re-derive this question.

  uv run conformance/documents/run.py . --json-only | python3 -c "import json,sys;[print(f['file'],'->',f['detail']) for x in json.load(sys.stdin)['results'] if x['rule']=='1b' for f in x['files']]"
