title: Pinned open: does an off-by-default drafting session count as the manager session in the hot path? (CVG-186)
description:
Contract: experience-collaboration.v1 Core 7 — "**The manager session is not in the hot path.** A write made in the app goes through the ordinary repository and proposal mechanism directly; the manager session learns of it as an event and folds it into its next turn."

Measured 2026-09-04 (converge-dgc, the reconcile after wave 8). `app/writes.py` now has two `subprocess.run(` sites, not one:

  line 258  ["git", *args]                                    — the repository write
  line 451  ["amplifier", "run", "--mode", "single", ...]      — draft_with_amplifier, DRAFT_TIMEOUT = 240.0

The second is reached from `record_ask()` only when `drafter == "agent"` (app/writes.py:656), and the only caller sets it from `ASK_DRAFTER = os.environ.get("CONVERGE_ASK_DRAFTER", "fixture")` (app/serve.py:38). So it is OFF as shipped, and ON with one environment variable — at which point the ask write blocks on a headless Amplifier session for up to four minutes before the proposal file is written.

Neither of the two readings converge-76y named is clean, which is why CVG-186 was re-derived to OPEN-PINNED rather than forced either way:

(a) KEPT, probe too narrow. A headless `amplifier run --mode single` is not *the* manager session: it is unregistered, has no steward (Core 8), and is discarded after one turn. Textually the clause is about the manager session, and no manager session is reached.

(b) BROKEN. The property the clause exists to protect is in its own kit assert — "A write made in the app lands through the repository mechanism without waiting for a manager turn." With the switch on, the ask write waits on an agent turn. Whether that agent is called the manager session is a naming question; the waiting is real.

THE DECISION THIS NEEDS, in one sentence: does clause 7 forbid *the manager session* in the write path, or *any* agent turn a write waits on? If the former, CVG-186 becomes CONFORMS and clause 7 should say so explicitly, because the current wording cannot be read off the code. If the latter, either the drafter goes or clause 7 gets a CANDIDATE amendment permitting an explicitly-switched-on, timeout-bounded drafting session whose failure still lands the write.

Not settled here because this lane owns `ledger/**` and `contracts/experience.v1-candidate.md` only — clause 7 lives in experience-collaboration.v1, whose candidate this lane may not author, and `app/writes.py` is another lane's file. CVG-186 asserts the current behaviour without forging the decision (PROTOCOL §3.3 OPEN-PINNED); its probe flips red if the default flips to "agent", if the gate disappears, if a third process appears, or if the second process stops being the drafting session — each break observed firing on a scratch copy 2026-09-04.

Related: converge-76y (the red-on-main report this answers).
acceptance: GIVEN the steward's ruling on which reading of clause 7 stands WHEN CVG-186 is re-derived THEN it carries CONFORMS or VIOLATION rather than OPEN-PINNED, and the clause wording (or the app's write path) has moved so the disposition can be read off the code without the ruling. description:
`experience-collaboration.v1` fixes the seam between two parties: git is the protocol, the host carries the conversation, and Converge renders it. Half of that seam is kept today and half does not exist. Measured 2026-09-04 against the app at 127.0.0.1:8823 by `conformance/experience-collaboration/run.py` — PASS 7 · FAIL 5 · SKIP 2.

**Kept, and worth saying so:** every write reaches the repository through git and nothing else (Core 1); no route and no line of app code addresses a second manager session (Core 2); one review renderer lays out every proposal with the origin as a value rather than a branch (Core 3); the answer lands in the dated ratification record (Core 5a); no write goes through the manager session (Core 7); a ratification is an ordinary commit with a sibling `*-candidate.md` beside the document (Core 9); no second collaboration surface has grown (Core 10).

**The four that fail, all one missing half — Converge never reaches the host:**

- **Core 4a** — nothing can carry a question to the host as a comment. No route addresses a pull request or its comments; no code path posts one. A steward asking a question has to leave and say it somewhere else, which is the copying between tools the clause exists to stop.
- **Core 5b** — the steward's word is recorded but nothing posts it back where the proposal came from. A teammate who proposed on the host learns the answer only if a person copies it across.
- **Core 6a / 6b** — nothing brings an inbound change in on its own: no webhook route, no live stream, no timer that reloads the project's data. Freshness is the steward's job — they find out by reloading. And nothing on the surface names a mechanism either, so a reader cannot tell whether what they are looking at is current. (6b is derived from 6a: there is no mechanism to name.)
- **Core 8a** — no manager session names a steward, so whose word counts is inferred from whoever is signed in (this target answered as `bkrabach`). The clause asks for it to be settled when the session is registered; everyone else is a teammate, whose proposals get the same reading and none of the authority.

The two halves that genuinely need a second party on a live host — a teammate's reply coming back attributed (4b), and no second person's word reaching the record (8b) — SKIP with that reason stated.

4a, 5b and 6a are one piece of work: a path to the repository host. 8a is separable and much smaller — a field on the manager registration.
acceptance: GIVEN the app is running WHEN `uv run conformance/experience-collaboration/run.py <app>` is run THEN rules 4a, 5b, 6a, 6b and 8a each PASS: a question can reach the host as a comment, the steward's word is posted back to its origin, inbound changes arrive without the steward acting, the app names in plain words how it stays fresh, and each manager session names exactly one steward settled at registration.

description:

Lane w8-collab-bridge added a sixth surface (`app/collab.py` plus the `collab.html` partial) and could not document it: `app/README.md` is outside that lane's file ownership.

What a paragraph there should say, so nobody has to read the code to find it out:

- **From the host** — open pull requests read with `gh pr list` / `gh pr view` in each of the manager session's repositories, laid out in the same proposal shape a `*-candidate.md` file produces, so the review anatomy is identical whatever the origin.
- **The routes** — `GET /api/collab/{mid}/pulls`, `GET /api/collab/{mid}/pulls/{number}`, `POST /api/collab/{mid}/pulls/{number}/comments`, `POST /api/collab/{mid}/pulls/{number}/answer`, `POST /api/collab/webhooks/host`, `GET /api/collab/{mid}/freshness`.
- **Answering writes twice, and reports both** — `app/writes.py` appends the word to `docs/workflow/owner-ratifications-<date>.md`, and the same word is posted to the pull request as a comment. The response carries `recorded` and `returnedToOrigin` separately, so a host that refuses the comment never makes the record look unwritten.
- **Freshness** — a webhook when the host can call one, polling every 60 seconds otherwise, and the panel prints which of the two is carrying it. Today it is polling: the webhook path is behind the sign-in gate (see the item about `PUBLIC_PREFIXES`).
- **Nothing is kept here** — no pull request, comment or answer is stored by the app; the only state is when the host last called, in memory, so a restart goes back to saying polling rather than claiming a webhook it has not heard from.
- **`gh` is required** for this surface and this surface only. Without it the panel says so in plain words rather than showing an empty list.
acceptance: GIVEN a reader opening `app/README.md` WHEN they look for the host panel THEN a section names its routes, both halves of what answering writes, which freshness mechanism is in use and why, that nothing about the conversation is stored, and that `gh` is required — the same depth every other surface's section has.
